cards.title: Your waiting room isn't a railway platform
cards.body: Crowded benches, repeated questions, files going missing. Most of the chaos comes from a few fixable habits, not just too many patients.

cards.title: 1. Tell people where they stand
cards.body: A simple token board, or a message with queue position, cuts down the constant 'kitna time lagega?' questions at the front desk.

cards.title: 2. Collect basics while they wait
cards.body: Reception can note weight, BP and the main complaint before the consult. The doctor starts with information instead of starting from zero.

cards.title: 3. Ask patients to bring their medicines
cards.body: A reminder message the day before: bring all current medicines and the last prescription. Fewer 'woh white wali goli' moments in the room.

cards.title: 4. Separate quick visits from long ones
cards.body: Report shows and short follow-ups can be grouped into a fixed slot. New, complex cases get time without blocking everyone else.

cards.title: 5. Give clear exit instructions
cards.body: A printed or messaged summary of next steps means fewer patients walking back to the desk confused about tests, timings or review dates.

cards.title: Calmer room, better consults
cards.body: Small process changes free up the doctor's minutes. AICA is building patient summaries that reach the clinic before the visit, with pilots in Lucknow.

takeaway: Queue updates, early basics, medicine reminders, separate slots and clear exit notes make a calmer waiting room.
share: For clinic staff: five simple fixes for waiting-room chaos. Worth a read.
